newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ING says prefers 20% in merged Belgian bank.
newsitem.headline: ING says prefers 20% in merged Belgian bank.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING would rather have 20 percent in a merged bank formed out of Belgian BBL and Generale Bank than continue to hold 20 percent in just BBL, Belgian newspaper La Libre Belgique quoted ING as saying.

Commenting that BBL (Banque Bruxelles Lambert) and Generale suffered from a weak presence abroad, the paper said ING chief executive officer Aad Jacobs said in Brussels on Thursday he preferred to have 20 percent in such a merged bank over nothing in BBL.

Plans for a merger between BBL and Generale first surfaced early last year and re-emerged this year, but the idea remained stillborn due to opposition from ING which does not want the merger to lead to a dilution of its stake in BBL.
In that respect Jacobs' position is unchanged, but his cautious preference for a merger between the two Belgian banks indicates he might now be more open to the idea itself.

"We have 20 percent of the voting rights. We are very happy with this stake. We do not want a merger between BBL and Generale Bank if we do not have the same influence and if our stake falls to eight percent," the paper quoted him as saying.

Asked if he did not expect to be treated "more decently" by the other shareholders in BBL now that control over Generale Bank was changing, Jacobs said that it was too early to speculate about facts "which have not yet been discussed by the executive board."
Generale Bank is controlled by Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA, whose French parent, Compagnie de Suez, is merging with French utilities company Lyonnaise des Eaux.
Jacobs said Generale, and Fortis, were no longer strategic priorities for the new group.
"That is an important point," he said. For now he had adopted a wait-and-see attitude.

Jacobs, who was speaking at a presentation on ING's 1996 results, said the one thing that was certain was that ING, which was sure it would recover the shares of the Lefebvre family in 1998, would not make a public offer for BBL.

ING, BBL's largest single shareholder, has a 12.04 percent stake and controls the voting rights on a 6.96 percent stake held by Befco Investments, a company belonging to Italian family Lefebvre. ING finances the Befco shares under a deal which ends in 1998.
